articleMarkdown:
# Studying Guài (Resolution): making the grounds and limits of a decision clear

When an issue needs a definite response, state the facts and your position clearly; decisiveness does not need impulse or coercion to prove itself.

A long-ambiguous situation sometimes does require a decision. Guài discusses public explanation, calls for attention, and removing obstacles, yet its statement explicitly says that resorting to arms is unfavorable. It does not equate firmness with violence or humiliation, instead directing attention to the risks and manner of action.

## Identity and line order

Guài is hexagram 43 in the traditional King Wen sequence, with symbol ䷪. The lower trigram is Qián ☰ and the upper trigram is Duì ☱; their traditional images are heaven and lake, respectively. Count the lines from the bottom: 初九、九二、九三、九四、九五、上六. A solid line is yang and a broken line is yin. Nine and six in the line labels designate yang and yin; they are not additional line numbers.

```text
━━━━ ━━━━  上六
━━━━━━━━━  九五
━━━━━━━━━  九四
━━━━━━━━━  九三
━━━━━━━━━  九二
━━━━━━━━━  初九
```

## Hexagram statement

夬：揚于王庭，孚號，有厲，告自邑，不利即戎，利有攸往。

Original editorial rendering; not a quotation from Legge: Resolution: declare it at the royal court, calling with sincerity. There is danger. Make the announcement from one's own city. Resorting to arms is unfavorable; it is beneficial to have somewhere to go.

Legge explains the ancient political scene of publicly dealing with a guilty powerful minister at the royal court, retaining sincere proclamation, awareness of danger, and limits against immediate force. This historical interpretation cannot decide who is guilty in modern life.

A modern reflection asks how to clarify facts, the issue needing action, and the scope of a decision. The greater the impact of public expression, the more it needs evidence and suitable procedures. A hexagram cannot support an unverified accusation.

References: [zhouyi-43](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/夬&oldid=2405003), [legge1882-43](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

## Interpretations in the Ten Wings

The Commentary on the Judgment and the Commentary on the Images belong to the commentarial collection known as the Yìzhuàn, usually called the Ten Wings. Below, these commentaries are kept separate from the hexagram and line statements, followed by modern learning applications.

The Commentary on the Judgment explains Guài as decision and connects decision with harmony. The Commentary on the Images takes a lake above heaven and speaks of distributing benefits downward. Decision in the commentaries has more than a hard edge.

Today, combine firmness with respect: a decision can be clear and its explanation understandable to those involved. Listening to new evidence does not automatically weaken a position.

References: [zhouyi-43](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/夬&oldid=2405003), [hon-sep](https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/chinese-change/)

## The six lines, from bottom to top

### 初九 · Wanting to charge ahead still requires the right conditions

壯于前趾，往不勝為咎。

Original editorial rendering; not a quotation from Legge: Strength in the forward toes: going ahead without prevailing brings blame.

Legge reads the strong toes as relying on force to rush ahead yet failing to finish. It distinguishes wanting to move from being able to act appropriately.

Before publishing an important conclusion, check the facts and who will be affected. Strong emotion cannot fill an information gap.

References: [zhouyi-43](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/夬&oldid=2405003), [legge1882-43](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

### 九二 · Alertness and requests for help need specifics

惕號，莫夜有戎，勿恤。

Original editorial rendering; not a quotation from Legge: An alert cry; even if arms appear at dusk or night, do not be consumed by worry.

A warning cry and possible armed trouble at night belong to an ancient unsettled scene. Legge preserves the sense of preparation and calling for assistance.

Today, clarify in advance who needs to confirm what and how to make contact when things change. The line does not predict a nighttime attack or justify suspicion of people's motives based on a hexagram.

References: [zhouyi-43](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/夬&oldid=2405003), [legge1882-43](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

### 九三 · Firmness need not appear as overbearing aggression

壯于頄，有凶。君子夬夬，獨行遇雨，若濡有慍，无咎。

Original editorial rendering; not a quotation from Legge: Strength displayed in the cheekbones brings misfortune. The noble person resolves firmly; walking alone, meeting rain, soaked and resented, yet without blame.

Qiú concerns the face; Legge reads it as a forceful expression, followed by walking alone, encountering rain, and resentment. The ancient text does not make a fierce appearance the basis of sound decision.

Express disagreement through clear facts rather than dominating with volume or posture. Others' displeasure does not automatically prove you right; return to the evidence.

References: [zhouyi-43](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/夬&oldid=2405003), [legge1882-43](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

### 九四 · When stuck, do not shut out useful advice

臀无膚，其行次且。牽羊悔亡，聞言不信。

Original editorial rendering; not a quotation from Legge: The buttocks have no skin; walking is hesitant. Led by a sheep, regret disappears. Hearing words, yet not believing.

Injured flesh and halting movement are harsh ancient images; Legge also considers unwillingness to accept suitable guidance. They must not become predictions about an actual body.

If your approach is plainly failing, listen to advice supported by reasons. Accepting help with one step does not surrender all judgment, and preserving appearances is not reason to refuse adjustment.

References: [zhouyi-43](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/夬&oldid=2405003), [legge1882-43](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

### 九五 · Retain a balanced standard while dealing with a problem

莧陸夬夬，中行无咎。

Original editorial rendering; not a quotation from Legge: Amaranth-like growth: resolve firmly. A central course brings no blame.

Legge interprets xiàn lù through plant imagery, linking decision with the central position while acknowledging that the symbolism is difficult to arrange. The plant's identification should not be presented as undisputed.

A modern analogy is taking limited action on a clear problem, without rejecting everyone connected to it or everything resembling it. Explicit scope makes a decision more responsible.

References: [zhouyi-43](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/夬&oldid=2405003), [legge1882-43](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

### 上六 · Losing channels of response also needs attention

无號，終有凶。

Original editorial rendering; not a quotation from Legge: No cry for help; misfortune in the end.

Legge reads the final absence of a cry as isolation, with nobody to call on for help. It is not a prediction that the reader will be abandoned.

When deciding, preserve necessary explanations and communication channels. If already isolated, seek trustworthy outside assistance rather than treating an unfavorable ancient statement as proof that no path remains.

References: [zhouyi-43](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/夬&oldid=2405003), [legge1882-43](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

## Clarifying a collaboration that can no longer remain vague

Original modern scenario

A project repeatedly acquires tasks never agreed upon, so its lead decides to reset the scope. She lists the original agreement, subsequent changes, and available resources, then discusses what must remain and what needs separate arrangements with those involved.

She does not speculate in a public group chat about who is deliberately taking advantage, nor reject new information merely because she intends to set a boundary. The final decision has clear grounds and an implementation method; unresolved matters remain recorded.

Guài here helps end ambiguity rather than turn cooperation into a battlefield for settling scores.

## Misreadings to avoid

- Guài cannot authorize unverified public accusations, revenge, or force. The ancient political scene of removing guilt does not entitle individuals to act as their own court.

- Decisiveness does not guarantee success and never justifies manufacturing isolation, threats, or humiliation to force agreement.

## Three practices

1. Describe the matter requiring a clear response in terms of verifiable facts and scope.

2. Identify one relevant piece of information you still need to hear, so decision does not become refusal of facts.

3. Choose suitable recipients and a suitable way to explain, reducing unnecessary public harm.

## Related hexagram

### Gòu — Encounter (hexagram-44)

Guài concerns a situation already identified as requiring action; Gòu concerns recognizing new encounters and establishing boundaries. Decisions and acceptance both require actual grounds.

## A closing question

While reading Guài, ask: can I clearly explain what needs addressing without portraying someone as an enemy to support the decision?
